sophia.kuo: Heads-up — ran a focused RoPE variant sweep across Llama-2-13B and Mixtral-7B (linear / NTK / YARN-damped). Found a consistent perplexity/quality bump on Mixtral around ~32k tokens for NTK and YARN variants when head_kv_dim was reduced.
andre.gomez: Can you paste the perf profile and the exact configs you used?
sophia.kuo: Quick paste from the internal run (summarized):
```
model: mixtral-7b
variant: ntk-scale
context: 32768
head_kv_dim: 64 (vs default 128)
batching: continuous, max_batch_tokens=2048
kernel: matmul_fused_v2
mean_latency: 42ms/token
ppl: baseline 1.12 -> 1.41 at ~32k tokens
kv_hit_ratio: 0.87 -> 0.62 after window slide/eviction
memcpy: spiky increases at eviction points
```
rajiv.patel: kv_hit_ratio drop + memcpy spikes sounds like eviction churn. Was KV stored packed or split across buffers when head_kv_dim != aligned size?
sophia.kuo: Yes — when head_kv_dim is 64 we end up packing two kv slots per native wordlane which forces the runtime to allocate a secondary buffer and trigger more frequent copy+compact operations. That increases eviction frequency and also interacts poorly with our prefix caching heuristic.
matthew.lewis: Also note continuous batching interacts: small batches cause earlier flushes of KV shards which compounds the eviction. Could be a batching * kernel interaction.
elaine.kim: Can we force the attention kernel to fallback to generic_attention for that case and see if the ppl spike persists? If optimized kernel assumes aligned head_kv layout it might be corrupting numeric behaviour under NTK scaling.
ci-bot: CI: benchmark job 42678 enqueued (perf/regression) — https://ci.redwood.ai/job/42678
andre.gomez: Also re-run with prefix caching disabled to isolate kv eviction vs ropeg scaling math.
sophia.kuo: Plan of action: 1) repro with head_kv_dim aligned to 128 (should remove packing edge-case) 2) run kernel fallback to generic_attention for NTK/YARN variants 3) nvprof to capture memcpy timelines + kernel dispatches 4) test YARN damping 0.7/0.85 to see if amplitude scales the quality bump 5) add a micro-benchmark that simulates the packing layout and eviction cadence. I'll open a tiny PR that toggles head_kv_dim and kernel fallback flags for quick A/B.
rajiv.patel: If repros are stable, let's add a per-model "safe head_kv range" table to model profiles so deploys know which dims to avoid by default.
sophia.kuo: Filed INF ticket with artifacts: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-789 — added nvprof crumbs and the raw log tarball.
andre.gomez: Great. If anyone else sees similar cliffs on Llama variants, ping here. Could be a general packing + RoPE scaling interaction rather than mixtral-only.
sophia.kuo: Thanks — will post short summary and a link to the PR once it's up. :memo:
